# THAF -- PUBLISH CONTENT GATE EXCEPTIONS  (narrow, documented, version-controlled)
#
# One line per exception:
#     <exact repo path> :: <pattern key> :: <reason>
#
# RULES, enforced by the gate's own self-test controls E1-E3:
#   * exact paths only -- no globs, no prefixes, no directories
#   * one pattern key per line, so an exception cannot excuse a file wholesale
#   * a second file carrying the same text is still refused
#
# This is the ONLY escape hatch. It is a text file rather than JSON because a
# .json anywhere in the published tree is refused by the path gate, and an
# escape hatch that changes how the guard behaves must not be able to hide.
#
# WHAT QUALIFIES
#   A page that is deliberately public technical instruction and has to name an
#   internal artefact to be intelligible -- for example a standards page that
#   documents this publication process and therefore has to describe the gate.
#   The exception must name the single page and the single pattern class.
#
# WHAT DOES NOT QUALIFY
#   Generator stamps left behind by a build script. Slack. "It is easier."
#   A page that mentions an internal tool because nobody removed the sentence.
#
# CURRENTLY ACTIVE: none.
#
# The gate is documented in the public standards page by DESCRIPTION, not by
# filename, so no exception is needed today. If one ever is added, the reason
# field is mandatory and is committed in the same public repository, i.e. visible
# to the reader it affects.
